results.reasoning: Judged on the review screen against a scratch copy served on 4722 from inside the copy with its own home, with a second project declared in that copy so the server really did have siblings to not offer. The bar carries exactly the session-level controls the statement claims and nothing about the rule in hand: the project name, the screen picker, the Prototype/App slider and Pin mode. `panel.blueprint` reads "walkdown" as dim inert text beside the wordmark - a SPAN with tabIndex -1, no role, no handler, not inside a button; clicking it changed nothing on screen and left the panel's markup byte-identical, while the Blueprints tab does hold the actual chooser, listing walkdown and the sibling as radio options (01-03). `panel.screen-picker` reads "The review page" closed, so the screen is legible without opening anything, and opening it shows `panel.screens-list` with "Detect from the page" plus every storyboard screen (06). Picking Rule detail by hand moved both surfaces to that screen and visibly re-styled the control - a cyan outlined button titled "Screen picked by hand", against the plain ghost text of detection - and the reopened list marks the picked row (07, 08); choosing "Detect from the page" drops it back to the ghost style and the detected title (09). Detection reports rather than remembers: with the picker left detecting, opening a rule whose screen is review navigated the page back from rule-detail, the bar label changed from "Rule detail (state...)" to "The review page" on its own, and the reopened list's mark moved with it, from "Detect from the page rule-detail" to "Detect from the page review" (11, 14, 15 and probe lines B/C/D). The slider swaps which surface the page area draws - the review mockup for Prototype, the base_url page for App (04, 05) - and Pin mode toggles on and off in place, amber when armed and outlined when not (12, 13). Caveats a reader should have: the App surface here is the run's base_url on 4700, which answered with a stand-in placeholder rather than a built page, so the App evidence shows the swap happening and not a rendered app; and file 10 is named for a move that had not happened yet, which the probe file says out loud. Nothing in the statement went unexercised, so this is a pass.
